key_insight: The paper introduces accelerated Lagrange-multiplier optimization flows that use second-order dynamics and variable splitting to maintain pseudo-energy dissipation while improving convergence on nonconvex problems.
engineering_relevance: These methods can make training more stable and less sensitive to learning-rate choices in scientific machine learning, especially for PINNs and DeepONets solving PDE-related tasks.
method: Linear LM-based second-order flow for unconstrained nonconvex optimization.
Linear LM-based variable/operator splitting to accelerate updates and improve stability.
Relaxed and adaptive variants to avoid multiplier degeneration and automatically adjust step size.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive numerical experiments on function optimization and PDE benchmarks, including PINNs and DeepONets, showing better local-minima escape, high accuracy, and strong robustness to initial learning rate.
watch_item: The approach relies on careful tuning of the second-order flow and multiplier updates, so implementation stability may depend on discretization choices and problem structure.
paper_title: Several Accelerated and Stable Pseudo-Energy-Dissipative Lagrange Multiplier Methods based on Second-order Flow and Variable Splitting
